fields.meta_description: See four drip campaign examples that start and stop on events in your own records, from a welcome series to unsubscribes. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Drip Campaign Around the Events in Your Own Data
fields.hero_description: Get a drip campaign that sends each email on schedule and pulls people out when they upgrade, book, or unsubscribe.
fields.features_heading: The Parts of a Drip Campaign Emergent Builds
fields.features_subheading: A drip campaign sends a pre-written series of messages over time, each one timed from an action the person took.
fields.feature_1:
Triggers read from your own records

Emergent builds the sequence on top of the records you already keep. A new signup, a trial start, or an open-house sign-in becomes the event that enrolls a contact in it.
fields.feature_2:
Delays written as plain sentences

Describe the timing the way you would tell a colleague: the first email at once, the next one 3 days later. To move a step, write the new timing and Emergent rebuilds it.
fields.feature_3:
Exit rules that end the sequence

Each sequence carries a list of events that take a contact out of it. A purchase or a booked call removes the contact from the sequence before the next scheduled email goes out.
fields.feature_4:
Sending through the services you connect

The app connects through its API to the email or SMS service you already use. Your sender and templates stay put, and the app decides which contact gets which message when.
fields.feature_5:
A contact history you own

Every enrollment and every exit is written to a database you own, along with each queued email. Open any contact to see which sequences they are in and the next email due.
fields.feature_6:
No task cap on large imports

The automation has no task cap. A 20,000-contact import walks through the same steps as a list of 20, and the welcome emails go out on the same schedule for every contact.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Drip Campaigns Worth Building First
fields.tab_content_1:
Welcome emails on day 0, day 3, and day 7

Ines Valcourt joins the Larkspur Ceramics newsletter from the studio's homepage, and the class schedule reaches her inbox that same minute. On day 3 she gets a note on the beginner wheel class. The third email lands on day 7 with $15 off her first class, and the series ends there.
fields.tab_content_2:
An upgrade on day 9 cancels the day 12 email

Bram Okafor starts a 14-day trial of Tallyhouse, an invoicing app, and still has no invoice sent by day 3. The app emails him a short guide to sending his first one. He upgrades to a paid plan on day 9, so the trial-ending email set for day 12 is canceled before it goes out.
fields.tab_content_3:
When she books a showing, the listings stop

Soledad Arriaga signs in at the open house at 14 Wren Lane and asks for homes under $450,000 in her zip code. Every Thursday for 6 weeks she is due the new listings that match. In week 2 she clicks Book a showing, her 4 remaining emails are canceled, and agent Dmitri Halvorsen gets a Slack message.
fields.tab_content_4:
One unsubscribe clears all 3 sequences

Wendell Achebe clicks unsubscribe at the foot of a Copperline Bikes service reminder. The app takes him out of all 3 sequences he was in, cancels the 4 emails still queued for him, and marks him Unsubscribed with the date and time. The next list import skips him.

fields.howto_title: How to Build a Drip Campaign
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan a drip campaign, write its emails and exits, and test the full sequence before real contacts enroll.
fields.howto_step_1_des: Choose one event your records already capture: a signup, a trial start, or a name on an open-house sheet. Starting from a recorded event means nobody has to tag contacts by hand before the first email.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Decide what a contact should do by the last email, such as book a class or upgrade. That action becomes the first exit. A person who takes it early stops getting emails that ask for it.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Give each email one point and one link, and send the first within a minute of the trigger. Leave a few days between the rest; a 7-day welcome series fits three emails without crowding the inbox.
fields.howto_step_4_des: The FTC's CAN-SPAM guide says each message must explain how the recipient can opt out and must include your valid physical postal address. Put both in the footer template once and every email carries them.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Write the trigger, the day each email goes out, and every exit as plain sentences in one prompt. Emergent builds the sequence and its contact records, plus a screen that shows who sits in which step.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Connect the email service you already send from, then import 50 contacts before the full list. Check that the first sends arrive and that each one enrolled on the right day.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Enroll a test contact with the delays shortened to minutes and read each email on a phone. Then trigger an exit and confirm the next scheduled email never goes out.

faq_plan.q: What is a drip campaign in marketing?
faq_plan.ref: What is a drip campaign in marketing?

prov.original: What is a drip campaign in marketing?

faq_plan.a: In marketing, a drip campaign is a pre-written series of messages sent to one person over time, each timed from something they did, such as joining a list. Mailchimp's glossary puts it as automated marketing emails sent to people who take specific actions on your website. Drip campaign marketing works best when every message has one job and one link.

faq_plan.q: How to create a drip campaign?
faq_plan.ref: How to create a drip campaign?

prov.original: How to create a drip campaign?

faq_plan.a: Create a drip campaign by settling the trigger first, then the emails and their send days, then the events that end it early. A drip campaign template can suggest timing, but the trigger and exits come from your own records. Emergent's AI automation builder turns those parts, written as sentences, into a working sequence.

A drip campaign is an automated series of messages that a person receives one at a time over days or weeks, starting after an action such as a signup. Wikipedia describes drip marketing as a strategy that sends, or drips, a pre-written set of messages over time. That pace is the whole drip campaign meaning: small messages on a schedule instead of one long one.

faq_plan.q: What is an example of a drip campaign?
faq_plan.ref: What is an example of a drip campaign?

prov.original: What is an example of a drip campaign?

faq_plan.a: An abandoned cart sequence is a common example: a shopper who leaves items in the cart gets a reminder an hour later and another the next day. Other drip campaign examples are course onboarding emails and renewal prompts. Each message reaches one person on their own timeline, unlike social media automation, where one post reaches a whole audience.

faq_plan.q: What is the best software for sending email drip campaigns?
faq_plan.ref: What is the best software for sending email drip campaigns?

prov.original: What is the best software for sending email drip campaigns?

faq_plan.a: The best software is the one that already holds your contacts and can start a sequence from the events you care about. For drip email campaigns, confirm it can trigger on your own data, end a sequence at the goal, and honor an unsubscribe across every sequence. When the trigger lives in your product data, Emergent builds the sequence on that data.

faq_plan.q: How do you create a real estate email drip campaign?
faq_plan.ref: how to create a real estate email drip campaign
faq_plan.a: Create a real estate email drip campaign by splitting leads by source first, because a buyer from an open house and a seller asking for a home value need different emails. Send buyers new listings inside their price limit on a fixed weekday, and send sellers a monthly note on nearby sales. End either drip the moment the lead books a showing or asks for a listing appointment.

faq_plan.q: What is a drip campaign in real estate?
faq_plan.ref: what is a drip campaign in real estate
faq_plan.a: In real estate, a drip campaign is a scheduled series of emails or texts that keeps an agent in touch with a lead before a showing or listing appointment. Agents run drip campaigns for leads not ready to talk yet. Once a lead replies or books, stop the drip and move the lead into the agent's sales automation.

faq_plan.q: What is a drip campaign in email marketing?
faq_plan.ref: what is a drip campaign in email marketing
faq_plan.a: In email marketing, a drip campaign is a sequence that starts separately for each subscriber on the day they act, rather than a single send to the whole list. A newsletter reaches everyone on one morning. A drip email campaign reaches one subscriber on day 1, another on day 4, and checks each contact's record before every send to see whether an exit has fired.

faq_plan.q: How do you create an email drip campaign?
faq_plan.ref: how to create email drip campaign
faq_plan.a: Create an email drip campaign by writing every email as a set before you schedule any of them. Give each one a single point and one link, then read the series in order to catch repeats. Keep email drip campaigns short at first and add messages once you see where people exit. Emergent can build the sequence from a prompt.

faq_plan.q: How do I create an SMS drip campaign?
faq_plan.ref: how do i create an sms drip campaign
faq_plan.a: Create an SMS drip campaign the same way as an email one, and get each person's consent to texts before the first message. Wikipedia notes that drip messages take the form of email, although other media can also be used. Collect the number and consent on a campaign landing page; that signup then starts the drip marketing campaign.

plan.angle: The top 10 are email platforms and glossaries that define the term and sell their own sender. This page shows four drip campaigns as working screens, each started and stopped by events in the business's own records: a three-email welcome series over 7 days, a trial-ending email canceled when the user upgrades, a weekly listings email for an open-house lead that ends when she books a showing, and one unsubscribe that clears every sequence. The FAQ covers the definitions, examples, real estate, and email and SMS setup that searchers compare.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Drip Campaign Around the Events in Your Own Data'; hero 'Get a drip campaign that sends each email on schedule and pulls people out when they upgrade, book, or unsubscribe.' covers the whole job: timing, enrolment and exits.

intent.evidence: Informational SERP (Mailchimp, Salesforce, Wikipedia glossaries; PAA on meaning, examples, how to start) is met: definition in features_subheading and FAQ 1/3/8, four worked examples in the tabs ('Welcome emails on day 0, day 3, and day 7'), a 7-step how-to, and the best-software PAA answered.

specificity.evidence: Buyer vocabulary throughout: trigger event, exit rules, open-house sign-in, trial-ending email, CAN-SPAM footer ('must include your valid physical postal address'); table uses the automation library.

openers.evidence: Paragraphs open on actions: 'Ines Valcourt joins the Larkspur Ceramics newsletter', 'Choose one event your records already capture', 'Every enrollment and every exit is written to a database you own'.

craft.evidence: Varied sentence length, one ', so' ending on the page ('He upgrades to a paid plan on day 9, so the trial-ending email ...'); no blocking craft defect.

voice.evidence: Concrete, unglamorous detail: '$15 off her first class', 'homes under $450,000 in her zip code', 'cancels the 4 emails still queued for him'; no hype vocabulary.

truth.evidence: Claims map to prompt-build, api-connect, database-owned, alerts, no-caps, free-start; third-party facts match their quoted spans (Mailchimp glossary, Wikipedia drip marketing, FTC CAN-SPAM guide: opt-out explanation and postal address). Tab numbers agree: 6 weekly emails, 2 sent, 4 canceled; 2+1+1 queued = 4 canceled.

distinct.evidence: Own angle (sequences started and ended by events in the business's records); no sibling primary in any heading; siblings only linked (social media automation, sales automation).

faq.evidence: 10 sourced questions (5 AlsoAsked, 5 Semrush questions), each answered in its first sentence, hub link in item 2, no brand or file format in any question.

images.evidence: Contact sheet matches copy: day 0/3/7 with 'Series ends, No fourth email'; 'Day 12: trial-ending email, Canceled'; 'Weeks 3 to 6, 4 emails canceled' with Slack card to Dmitri; 3 sequences 2+1+1 queued, '4 emails canceled'. One hero, cursors on buttons.
